clue.text: Basic drive in pool that pockets black one

indicators.note: a pool that pockets something holds it inside, as a snooker table pockets balls

parts.note: a lido is an open-air swimming pool
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A snooker player's basic urge in a game of pool is to pot the black.
explanation.walkthrough: The snooker picture of pockets and the black ball hides a swimming pool, LIDO, wrapped round B and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's term for the fundamental sexual or vital urge, so a basic drive.

clue.text: Praise surrounds bird heading range

indicators.note: the word for praise goes around the bird

parts.note: to laud is to praise
a tit is a small songbird
E for east is a compass heading

explanation.surface: Praise surrounds a bird as it flies across a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is scope or freedom of action, a synonym of range.

clue.text: One of two unions is great, one obscure

parts.note: big means great in size
a means one
to mist is to obscure or blur

explanation.surface: Of two marriages, one is great and the other kept dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a person in two marriages at once is party to both unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone married to two spouses at once is a party to two marriages.

clue.text: Some did it together just the same

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people acted together in exactly the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to say the same thing again, meaning likewise or just as before.

clue.text: Blade introduces a doctor to club

indicators.note: the club has the following letters introduced into its middle

parts.note: a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golf club

explanation.surface: A sword is brought in to show a doctor to a club.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOON as a golf club is an old usage: it was a wooden club with a lofted face.
explanation.definitionFit: A spadroon is a light cut-and-thrust sword, so a kind of blade.

clue.text: Planet earth — ET runs off to hide when finished

indicators.note: the alien runs off, but the letters run into a new order

explanation.surface: E.T. flees planet Earth to hide when he is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs off' rearranges PLANET EARTH plus ET; 'hide' is animal skin, not concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent leather is a hide given a glossy varnished finish.

clue.text: Separate night ends in gloomy quarter

indicators.note: the night's ends go inside the gloomy word

parts.note: dismal means gloomy

indicators.note: the first and last letters of night

parts.note: E for east is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A night spent apart in a gloomy part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes N and T from night; 'quarter' is a compass quarter, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take apart, so to separate into pieces.

clue.text: Moving it east-nor'-east

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges them

parts.note: nor' is short for north, taken here as its letters

explanation.surface: Setting a course east-north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: The compound bearing reads as one direction, but 'Moving' scrambles its first part, and only the last 'east' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is the East, as in the countries of Asia.

clue.text: Laymen slipped in another way

indicators.note: the laymen have slipped, so their letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Non-clergy slipped in by a different route.
explanation.definitionFit: Namely introduces a restatement, putting something in other words.

clue.text: Pointlessly hose drunk

indicators.note: without a point of the compass, here S for south, removed from the word

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights

explanation.surface: Someone drunk hoses things down without purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointlessly' takes off S, a compass point, from TIGHTS; hose as legwear, not a garden pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal slang for intoxicated, a common synonym for drunk.

clue.text: Contrary to the object of worship?

definitions.text: Contrary to the object of worship?

parts.words: Contrary to the object of worship?
parts.note: an object of worship turned round becomes the worship of an object, the contrary word order, which names a cult of revering things

explanation.surface: A question about opposing an idol.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'object of worship' reversed in order gives 'worship of the object', the practice of revering a charm or idol.
explanation.definitionFit: The practice of worshipping inanimate objects reverses the phrase 'object of worship' in sense.

clue.text: Alarm calls had to be paid for: a sign of what's to come

definitions.text: a sign of what's to come

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout, so warning calls are fores
owing means still to be paid for

explanation.surface: Warning cries that had to be paid for foretold trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the shout golfers give to warn others of a ball in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreshadowing is an advance hint or indication of something coming.

clue.text: French dance in place with shroud over pulpit

indicators.note: the city is laid over the pulpit, covering it on both sides

parts.note: Turin is the Italian city that holds the famous Shroud of Turin
an ambo is a raised pulpit or reading desk in early churches

explanation.surface: A dance performed in a town where a shroud hangs over the pulpit.
explanation.walkthrough: Turin is the Italian city famous for the Shroud of Turin; AMBO, a church lectern, sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambourin is a lively Provençal dance accompanied by a drum, hence a French dance.

clue.text: 17's first league record

parts.note: the first word of the heroine's name at 17 across, her forename

explanation.surface: The opening entry of a league's record book.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a yearly record of events, usually used in the plural.

clue.text: Unhappy that record is not played earlier?

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a record that is not played earlier is on so late, read as on plus so late

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable that their record didn't get played sooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DISC ON SO LATE: a record on so late is one not played earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconsolate means cheerless and beyond consolation, so very unhappy.

clue.text: Never been had?

parts.note: had in the sense of owned or possessed rather than cheated: something that has never belonged to anyone

explanation.definitionFit: Something without any possessor has never been owned, a cryptic twist on being had.

clue.text: One in the church?

indicators.note: one is placed inside the church

parts.note: a minster is a large church
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking who is a figure inside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: A whole-clue reading: I in MINSTER, and a minister is also one serving in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, someone who serves in the church.

clue.text: Window when framed by good joiner

indicators.note: the word for when is held within the joiner like a picture in a frame

parts.note: cement joins things firmly
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A window when fitted by a skilled carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a carpenter, but here it is something that joins, cement.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a window hinged at the side.

clue.text: Eponymous heroine has ones opposed to king in sporting stadium

parts.note: an means one, so two of them facing each other, one forwards and one backwards, give these letters
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: a stadium sporting something wears it, holding it within

parts.note: an arena is a sporting stadium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heroine joins the opponents of a king inside a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ones opposed' means one AN set against its mirror image; 'sporting' means the stadium wears the little word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's novel is named after its central character, so she is an eponymous heroine.

clue.text: What sheep go through and get up sluggish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: sheep are dipped in a sheep dip, a trough of disinfectant
rot is a disease sheep get, as in foot rot

explanation.surface: Sheep go through something and then get up slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DIP + ROT, both farming terms for sheep, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpid means sluggish and inactive, as in an animal in torpor.

clue.text: Time to put out light material

parts.note: to issue is to put out or publish

explanation.surface: Time to turn off a lamp's fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' suggests extinguishing a light, but it means publish, ISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is a thin gauzy fabric or paper, a light material.

clue.text: Pollarded more promising willow …

indicators.note: a pollarded tree has its top cut off, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: rosier means having brighter prospects, more promising

explanation.surface: A cut-back willow looks more hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pollarded' is apt for trees: it removes the head, R, from ROSIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a species of willow whose shoots are used in basketry.

clue.text: … or else pruned white rose

indicators.note: pruning reshapes the rose, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A white rose cut back, continuing the gardening of the clue before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pruned' shuffles the nine letters of WHITE ROSE; the ellipses link it to the willow clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise and or else both introduce an alternative or consequence, so are synonyms.

clue.text: Turn like the worm turned in Huckleberry Finn

indicators.note: the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters are found inside the name that follows

explanation.surface: Turning against authority, like Twain's boy hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The worm turns' means even the meek will fight back, so to turn like the worm is to rise up; the word sits backwards inside Huckleberry.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says even a worm will turn, that is, resist; to do so is to revolt.

clue.text: Hinder bill backing French king

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice or poster

indicators.note: the French word for king is read from the back

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A French monarch supports some legislation, which slows things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hinder' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning further back.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinder as an adjective means rear, and posterior also means situated behind.

clue.text: Swim and climb at health centre

indicators.note: the letters sit in the centre of the run of words climb at health, spanning them

explanation.surface: Someone swims and climbs at the local leisure centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to swim for pleasure in the sea or a pool.

clue.text: Get ready to time event

parts.note: to dress is to get ready, as in dressing for an occasion
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Advice to prepare so as to time a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is an equestrian competition, one of the events at horse trials.

clue.text: Small bloomer when knowledge is in short measure

indicators.note: the knowledge is placed inside the short measure

parts.note: ft is the short form of foot, a measure
lore is traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: A small mistake happens when knowledge is lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a flowering thing; FT is the abbreviation of foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A floret is one of the small flowers making up a composite flower head, so a tiny bloomer.
